patient_actor_hidden.History: The patient reports a 2-month history of fatigue and several episodes of lower abdominal pain. She expresses a strong belief that she has cancer and desires a diagnostic laparoscopy. The patient has been off work for 2 weeks on sick leave due to stress at work and wishes to return. She was diagnosed with peptic ulcer disease 6 months ago.

Secondary_Symptoms: Desire for diagnostic laparoscopy due to cancer concern

patient_actor_hidden.Social_History: Works as a nurse. No mention of smoking, alcohol use, or recreational drug use.
patient_actor_hidden.Review_of_Systems: Reports tiredness and depressed mood. No mention of changes in bowel or urinary habits.

objective_for_doctor: Evaluate and manage a patient presenting with fatigue, stress, and concern for cancer.

turns.doctor_opening: Hello, what brings you in today? Could you tell me about yourself and what's been going on?
turns.patient_opening: Doctor: Hello, what brings you in today? Could you tell me about yourself and what's been going on? Patient: I’m a 26-year-old nurse, and over the last two months I’ve had a lot of fatigue and a few episodes of lower abdominal pain. I’ve also been feeling very stressed at work and I’m worried it might be cancer, so I’d like to ask about diagnostic laparoscopy.

turns.doctor_question: Have you noticed any swelling in your joints?
turns.patient_answer: “Not that I’m aware of—no noticeable joint swelling, though I do feel generally run-down and tired. I haven’t had any changes in how my joints look or move.”

turns.doctor_question: Have you noticed any bumps, sores, or unusual spots on your scalp?
turns.patient_answer: “Not really—no bumps, sores, or unusual spots on my scalp that I’ve noticed. I’ve mainly just been feeling very tired and having occasional lower abdominal pain.”

turns.doctor_question: Have you been experiencing any itching or a sensation of itchiness lately?
turns.patient_answer: “Not really—no unusual itching or scratchy sensations lately. I’ve mainly been dealing with fatigue and occasional lower abdominal pain, plus a lot of stress from work.”

turns.doctor_question: Do you have any trouble lifting your arms above your head?
turns.patient_answer: “I can lift my arms above my head without much trouble—I haven’t noticed any weakness or specific problems with that.”

turns.doctor_question: Have you noticed any loss of vision that isn’t accompanied by pain?
turns.patient_answer: “No, I haven’t noticed any loss of vision or any vision changes like that—no, it hasn’t been happening.”

turns.doctor_question: Have you had a fever that’s felt extremely hot—like a temperature above 104 °F (40 °C) that’s made you feel dizzy or very uncomfortable?
turns.patient_answer: “No—I haven’t had any fever like that, and I don’t feel dizzy or extremely uncomfortable from a high temperature. It’s mostly been ongoing fatigue and the occasional lower abdominal pain.”

turns.doctor_question: Have you been feeling unusually stressed or overwhelmed lately?
turns.patient_answer: “Yes, I’ve been unusually stressed and overwhelmed lately—work has been weighing on me a lot, and I’ve been off sick for about two weeks because I felt I couldn’t cope. With the fatigue and abdominal pain, I’ve been increasingly worried something serious might be going on, possibly cancer, and I want to get the right diagnostic checks.

turns.doctor_question: Have you experienced any burning or discomfort when you urinate?
turns.patient_answer: “Not that I’ve noticed—there’s been no burning or discomfort when I urinate. It’s mainly the fatigue and the occasional lower abdominal pain, along with feeling very stressed at work.”

turns.doctor_question: Have you been feeling chills lately?
turns.patient_answer: “No, I haven’t had chills or felt like I was shaking with cold—mostly it’s just the fatigue, the occasional lower abdominal pain, and feeling overwhelmed and worried about what could be causing it.”

turns.doctor_question: Have you noticed any lumps or masses in your breasts that feel fixed or don’t move?
turns.patient_answer: “No, I haven’t noticed any lumps or masses in my breasts that feel fixed or don’t move. I’ve mainly just been feeling very fatigued, with occasional lower abdominal pain and a lot of stress and worry about what it could be.”

turns.doctor_question: Have you been feeling any pain or discomfort on the side of your back or abdomen, between your ribs and hips?
turns.patient_answer: “I’ve had occasional lower abdominal pain, but I don’t really have pain on the sides of my back between my ribs and hips. Most of the discomfort is concentrated low in my abdomen rather than in that flank area.”

turns.doctor_question: Do you feel pain in your calf when you walk, and does it go away when you stop and rest?
turns.patient_answer: “No, I haven’t noticed any calf pain when I walk, and it doesn’t happen with walking or improve when I stop—I’ve mainly been dealing with fatigue, occasional lower abdominal pain, and feeling very stressed and worried.”

turns.doctor_question: Have you noticed that your urine looks darker than usual?
turns.patient_answer: “No, I haven’t noticed my urine looking darker than usual. It’s been mainly the fatigue, occasional lower abdominal pain, and feeling really overwhelmed and worried about what it could be.”

turns.doctor_question: Have you noticed any difficulty moving your arm up or across your body?
turns.patient_answer: “No, I haven’t noticed any difficulty moving my arms up or across my body—movement feels normal and I’m not having any weakness or pain with it.”

turns.doctor_question: Have you noticed that your joints feel sore or stiff after doing the same activity repeatedly, like after a long day of typing, lifting, or other repetitive motions?
turns.patient_answer: “No, I haven’t noticed any joint soreness or stiffness after repetitive activities—I haven’t had swelling, and my arms and movement feel normal. It’s mainly the fatigue, occasional lower abdominal pain, and the stress at work. I’m just worried because I’m concerned about what serious causes could be.”
